Fix an integer dimension $d\ge1$ and an integer resolution $N\ge2$, where
$N\in\mathbb N$ ([[def-natural-numbers]]), and put $h=1/N$. Real scalar and
array operations use the field $\mathbb R$ ([[thm-reals-field]]). Let
$J_N=\{0,\ldots,N-1\}^d$; each coordinate index addition below is reduced
to the unique element of $\{0,\ldots,N-1\}$ congruent modulo $N$. The unit
torus $\mathbb T^d$ means the unit cube with opposite faces identified, so
fields and arrays are periodic across those faces. Write
$\mathbf 1=(1,\ldots,1)$ and let $e_i$ be the $i$th standard coordinate vector.
Cell $j$ has centre $x_j=h(j+\tfrac12\mathbf 1)$. The pressure value $q_j$ is
stored at that centre. Velocity component $i$ is stored at the right face of
cell $j$, with centre $x_j+\tfrac h2e_i$.

Let $\widetilde Q_h$ be all real scalar cell arrays and let
$Q_h=\{q\in\widetilde Q_h:h^d\sum_jq_j=0\}$. Let $V_h$ be the real vector
face arrays $v=(v_{i,j})_{1\le i\le d,\,j\in J_N}$. Give them the mass inner products
$$ (q,r)_{Q_h}=h^d\sum_{j\in J_N}q_jr_j,\qquad (v,w)_{M_h}=h^d\sum_{i=1}^d\sum_{j\in J_N}v_{i,j}w_{i,j}. $$
Define the pressure gradient $G_h:\widetilde Q_h\to V_h$ and velocity
divergence $D_h:V_h\to Q_h$ by
$$ (G_hq)_{i,j}=\frac{q_{j+e_i}-q_j}{h},\qquad (D_hv)_j=\sum_{i=1}^d\frac{v_{i,j}-v_{i,j-e_i}}{h}. $$
The compatible pressure Laplacian is $\Delta_h=D_hG_h$; its restriction to
$Q_h$ is negative semidefinite, and $G_h$ annihilates constants. Define the
componentwise vector Laplacian by
$$ (\Delta_h^Vv)_{i,j}=h^{-2}\sum_{\ell=1}^d (v_{i,j+e_\ell}-2v_{i,j}+v_{i,j-e_\ell}),\qquad A_h=-\Delta_h^V, $$
and the discrete velocity-gradient seminorm by
$$ \|\mathcal G_hv\|_{M_h}^2=h^{d-2}\sum_{i=1}^d\sum_{\ell=1}^d\sum_{j\in J_N} |v_{i,j+e_\ell}-v_{i,j}|^2. $$
The fixed cell/face placement is part of the definition; collocated central
differences are a different discretization.

Let $T:V\to W$ be a linear map of vector spaces over $F$, with $V$
finite-dimensional. Then

$$\dim_F V=\operatorname{nullity}T+\operatorname{rank}T.$$

Equivalently,

$$\dim_F V=\dim_F(\ker T)+\dim_F(\operatorname{im}T).$$

For $x,y\in\mathbb R^n$ and $z,w\in\mathbb C^n$, the formulas

$$\langle x,y\rangle_{\mathbb R^n}=\sum_{k<n}x_ky_k,\qquad \langle z,w\rangle_{\mathbb C^n}=\sum_{k<n}z_k\overline{w_k}$$

define inner products, linear in the first argument. At $n=0$, the unique pairing on the zero space is an inner product.

For all vectors $x,y$ in a real or complex inner-product space,

$$|\langle x,y\rangle|\le\|x\|\,\|y\| ,$$

with equality if and only if $x$ and $y$ are linearly dependent.

derivations.claim: Reindexing the finite periodic sums gives, for every cell array $q$ and face array $v$, $$ (G_hq,v)_{M_h} =h^d\sum_{i,j}\frac{(q_{j+e_i}-q_j)v_{i,j}}h =-h^d\sum_jq_j\sum_i\frac{v_{i,j}-v_{i,j-e_i}}h =-h^d\sum_jq_j(D_hv)_j. $$ In particular, when $q\in Q_h$, this is $(G_hq,v)_{M_h}=-(q,D_hv)_{Q_h}$, the negative-adjoint identity in the stated mass pairings.

Let $q\in Q_h$. Since $q$ has mean zero, $$ q_x=N^{-d}\sum_{y\in J_N}(q_x-q_y), $$ and [F3]–[F4] give the finite-sum Cauchy--Schwarz inequality $$ \|q\|_{Q_h}^2\le N^{-2d}\sum_{x,y\in J_N}|q_x-q_y|^2. $$ For each ordered pair $(x,y)$ choose the path that changes coordinates in the order $1,\ldots,d$, moving forward modulo $N$ in each coordinate. It has at most $dN$ directed edges. Cauchy--Schwarz along the path bounds $|q_x-q_y|^2$ by $dN$ times the sum of squared edge differences on it.

For any cell array $q$, applying the explicit weighted-sum identity of step 1.1 with $v=G_hq$ gives $$ h^d\sum_jq_j(\Delta_hq)_j=-(G_hq,G_hq)_{M_h}\le0. $$ If $\Delta_hq=0$, then $G_hq=0$, so $q_{j+e_i}=q_j$ for every $i,j$. Coordinate steps connect all cells of the periodic grid, hence $q$ is constant. Every constant has zero gradient, so the kernel on all cell arrays is exactly the constants.

For every $v$, summing $D_hv$ over cells cancels each face value once with its opposite occurrence, so $D_hv$ has zero mean. The same is true of $\Delta_hq=D_h(G_hq)$. Therefore $\Delta_h$ restricts to a linear map $Q_h\to Q_h$. Its kernel there is zero by step 2.1, and its domain and codomain are the same finite-dimensional space.

Rank-nullity [F2] now gives $\dim\operatorname{im}\Delta_h=\dim Q_h$; since the image is a subspace of $Q_h$, the restriction is onto as well as one-to-one. Thus each mean-zero right-hand side has a unique mean-zero pressure solution.

Fix one directed edge in coordinate $i$. For each coordinate $r<i$, its value along the path is $y_r$; to use the fixed edge, $y_r$ is fixed and $x_r$ has at most $N$ choices. For each $r>i$, the path still has value $x_r$; then $x_r$ is fixed and $y_r$ has at most $N$ choices. In coordinate $i$ there are at most $N^2$ ordered start/end pairs. Hence this edge occurs in at most $N^{d+1}$ paths. Summing the path bounds and dividing by $N^{2d}$ yields $$ \|q\|_{Q_h}^2\le dN^{2-d}\sum_{i,j}|q_{j+e_i}-q_j|^2 =d\|G_hq\|_{M_h}^2. $$ Taking nonnegative square roots proves the stated inequality.

Let $n\ge0$, let $f$ have continuous derivatives through order $n+1$ on an
open interval containing the closed interval between $c$ and $x$, and define

Every function differentiable at $c$ is continuous at $c$.
If $f,g$ are real functions differentiable at $c$, then $f+g$ and $fg$ are

$$

derivations.claim: For $g\in C^3(\mathbb T^d)$, Taylor's formula with Lagrange remainder at the midpoint and [F3] with $m=2$ give $$ g(x+h e_i/2)-g(x-h e_i/2)=h\,\partial_i g(x)+r, \qquad |r|\le h^3\|\partial_i^3g\|_\infty/24. $$ The same midpoint formula, with the two cell centres surrounding face $x_j+he_i/2$, gives $$ (G_hR_hp)_{i,j}=\partial_i p(x_j+he_i/2)+O(h^2), $$ with the pointwise error bounded by $h^2\|\partial_i^3p\|_\infty/24$.

For $g\in C^4(\mathbb T^d)$, [F3] with $m=3$ at $x$ gives $$ g(x+h e_i)-2g(x)+g(x-h e_i)=h^2\partial_i^2g(x)+r, $$ where the two fourth-order Lagrange remainders have total absolute value at most $h^4\|\partial_i^4g\|_\infty/12$. Apply this in every coordinate to $u_i$ at its face centre. It follows that $(A_hR_hu)_{i,j}=-(\Delta u_i)(x_j+he_i/2)+O(h^2)$, with the error bounded by $h^2\sum_\ell\|\partial_\ell^4u_i\|_\infty/12$.

Applying the midpoint formula to component $u_i$ at cell centre $x_j$ shows, by [F3] with $m=2$, $$ (D_hR_hu)_j=\sum_i\partial_i u_i(x_j)+r_j, \qquad |r_j|\le\frac{h^2}{24}\sum_i\|\partial_i^3u_i\|_\infty. $$ Thus the discrete divergence differs pointwise from the sampled continuous divergence by $O(h^2)$.

Each pointwise error bound in steps 1.1–1.2 is uniform. The weighted mass of the grid contains $h^dN^d=1$ total cell volume and there are $d$ velocity components. Therefore the corresponding mass norms are bounded by the same constants (or their finite $d$-component sum) times $h^2$. Combining the divergence, vector Laplacian and pressure gradient bounds proves the first claim. The scalar mass norm is defined on all cell arrays, so no zero-mean hypothesis on the residual is needed.

On each cell centred at $x_j$, fix $x$ and put $z=x-x_j$ and $\psi(t)=g(x_j+tz)$ for $0\le t\le1$. By [F3] with $m=1$ and [F4], $g(x)=g(x_j)+\nabla g(x_j)\cdot z+r_j(x)$ with $|r_j(x)|\le C_d\|D^2g\|_\infty|z|^2$. The identity $$ 2(\widetilde u^{n+1}-u^n,\widetilde u^{n+1})_{M_h} =\|\widetilde u^{n+1}\|_{M_h}^2-\|u^n\|_{M_h}^2 +\|\widetilde u^{n+1}-u^n\|_{M_h}^2 $$ and [F4] give $$ \|\widetilde u^{n+1}\|_{M_h}^2-\|u^n\|_{M_h}^2 +\|\widetilde u^{n+1}-u^n\|_{M_h}^2 +2\nu k\|\mathcal G_h\widetilde u^{n+1}\|_{M_h}^2 +2k(G_hp^n,\widetilde u^{n+1})_{M_h} =2k(f^{n+1},\widetilde u^{n+1})_{M_h}. $$

By [F2] and the pressure equation in [F1], $$ 2k(G_hp^n,\widetilde u^{n+1})_{M_h} =-2k(p^n,D_h\widetilde u^{n+1})_{Q_h} =-2k^2(p^n,\Delta_h\phi^{n+1})_{Q_h} =2k^2(G_hp^n,G_h\phi^{n+1})_{M_h}. $$ The last equality follows from the second identity in [F2].

Since $P_h$ is orthogonal and $u^{n+1}=P_h\widetilde u^{n+1}$ by [F3], the projection residual $\widetilde u^{n+1}-u^{n+1}=kG_h\phi^{n+1}$ is orthogonal to $u^{n+1}$. Pythagoras gives $$ \|\widetilde u^{n+1}\|_{M_h}^2 =\|u^{n+1}\|_{M_h}^2+k^2\|G_h\phi^{n+1}\|_{M_h}^2. $$ The pressure update $p^{n+1}=p^n+\phi^{n+1}$ then gives $$ k^2\bigl(\|G_hp^{n+1}\|_{M_h}^2-\|G_hp^n\|_{M_h}^2\bigr) =k^2\|G_h\phi^{n+1}\|_{M_h}^2 +2k^2(G_hp^n,G_h\phi^{n+1})_{M_h}. $$
Substitute the two identities from step 3.1 into step 1.1, replacing $\|\widetilde u^{n+1}\|_{M_h}^2$ and the pressure cross term. The result is exactly the displayed modified energy identity.

On the grid of [[def-na-periodic-staggered-grid-stokes-operators]], let
$\Delta_h^{-1}:Q_h\to Q_h$ be the inverse from
[[lem-na-periodic-grid-pressure-laplacian-zero-mode-and-poincare]]. Define
$$ P_h:=I-G_h\Delta_h^{-1}D_h:V_h\to V_h. $$
Then $P_h$ is the mass-orthogonal projector onto
$Z_h=\ker D_h$. In the backward-Euler algorithm
[[alg-na-periodic-incremental-pressure-correction]], the velocity correction
satisfies $u^{n+1}=P_h\widetilde u^{n+1}$ and
$D_hu^{n+1}=0$ exactly.

On the periodic staggered grid of
[[def-na-periodic-staggered-grid-stokes-operators]], every admissible backward-
Euler step of [[alg-na-periodic-incremental-pressure-correction]] and every
admissible BDF2 step of
[[alg-na-bdf2-incremental-and-rotational-pressure-correction]] has a unique
predictor, a unique mean-zero pressure increment, and a unique updated pair.
Both algorithms preserve the zero-mean pressure gauge and exact discrete
incompressibility.

Use [[def-na-periodic-staggered-grid-stokes-operators]] with $h=1/N$. For a
smooth periodic vector field $u\in C^4(\mathbb T^d;\mathbb R^d)$, define
$R_hu$ by sampling component $i$ at each face centre $x_j+he_i/2$. For a
smooth periodic scalar $p\in C^3(\mathbb T^d)$, define $R_hp$ by sampling at
cell centres $x_j$. Put $\|r\|_{\widetilde Q_h}=(h^d\sum_jr_j^2)^{1/2}$ for all cell arrays $r$;
this agrees with $\|r\|_{Q_h}$ on $Q_h$. Then uniformly for $N\ge2$,
$$ \|D_hR_hu-R_h(\nabla\cdot u)\|_{\widetilde Q_h} +\|A_hR_hu-R_h(-\Delta u)\|_{M_h} +\|G_hR_hp-R_h(\nabla p)\|_{M_h} \le C h^2, $$
where $C$ depends only on $d$ and the suprema of the displayed fields'
derivatives through orders $4$ for $u$ and $3$ for $p$. Here the sampling of a
vector field is facewise componentwise. For any $g\in C^2(\mathbb T^d)$ with
zero integral, the cell-centred or face-centred midpoint samples have discrete
mean of absolute value at most $C_dh^2\|D^2g\|_\infty$.

Use the spaces and operators of
[[def-na-periodic-staggered-grid-stokes-operators]] with $d\ge1$, $N\ge2$,
and $h=1/N$. Then $\Delta_h=D_hG_h$ maps $Q_h$ bijectively to itself, the
kernel of $\Delta_h$ on all cell arrays consists exactly of the constants,
and $D_hv$ has zero mean for every $v\in V_h$. In addition, every $q\in Q_h$
satisfies the resolution-independent bound
$$ \|q\|_{Q_h}\le\sqrt d\,\|G_hq\|_{M_h}. $$

For all vectors $x,y$ in a real or complex inner-product space,

$$|\langle x,y\rangle|\le\|x\|\,\|y\| ,$$

with equality if and only if $x$ and $y$ are linearly dependent.

Fix an integer dimension $d\ge1$ and an integer resolution $N\ge2$, where
$N\in\mathbb N$ ([[def-natural-numbers]]), and put $h=1/N$. Real scalar and
array operations use the field $\mathbb R$ ([[thm-reals-field]]). Let
$J_N=\{0,\ldots,N-1\}^d$; each coordinate index addition below is reduced
to the unique element of $\{0,\ldots,N-1\}$ congruent modulo $N$. The unit
torus $\mathbb T^d$ means the unit cube with opposite faces identified, so
fields and arrays are periodic across those faces. Write
$\mathbf 1=(1,\ldots,1)$ and let $e_i$ be the $i$th standard coordinate vector.
Cell $j$ has centre $x_j=h(j+\tfrac12\mathbf 1)$. The pressure value $q_j$ is
stored at that centre. Velocity component $i$ is stored at the right face of
cell $j$, with centre $x_j+\tfrac h2e_i$.

Let $\widetilde Q_h$ be all real scalar cell arrays and let
$Q_h=\{q\in\widetilde Q_h:h^d\sum_jq_j=0\}$. Let $V_h$ be the real vector
face arrays $v=(v_{i,j})_{1\le i\le d,\,j\in J_N}$. Give them the mass inner products
$$ (q,r)_{Q_h}=h^d\sum_{j\in J_N}q_jr_j,\qquad (v,w)_{M_h}=h^d\sum_{i=1}^d\sum_{j\in J_N}v_{i,j}w_{i,j}. $$
Define the pressure gradient $G_h:\widetilde Q_h\to V_h$ and velocity
divergence $D_h:V_h\to Q_h$ by
$$ (G_hq)_{i,j}=\frac{q_{j+e_i}-q_j}{h},\qquad (D_hv)_j=\sum_{i=1}^d\frac{v_{i,j}-v_{i,j-e_i}}{h}. $$
The compatible pressure Laplacian is $\Delta_h=D_hG_h$; its restriction to
$Q_h$ is negative semidefinite, and $G_h$ annihilates constants. Define the
componentwise vector Laplacian by
$$ (\Delta_h^Vv)_{i,j}=h^{-2}\sum_{\ell=1}^d (v_{i,j+e_\ell}-2v_{i,j}+v_{i,j-e_\ell}),\qquad A_h=-\Delta_h^V, $$
and the discrete velocity-gradient seminorm by
$$ \|\mathcal G_hv\|_{M_h}^2=h^{d-2}\sum_{i=1}^d\sum_{\ell=1}^d\sum_{j\in J_N} |v_{i,j+e_\ell}-v_{i,j}|^2. $$
The fixed cell/face placement is part of the definition; collocated central
differences are a different discretization.

Let $m \in \mathbb{N}$ with $m \ge 1$ and let $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$ with $a < b$.

1. **Fundamental theorem, second part, in $\mathbb{R}^{m}$.** Let
   $f : [a,b] \to \mathbb{R}^{m}$ be differentiable at every point of $[a,b]$ as
   a function on $[a,b]$ ([[def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral]]), and
   suppose $f' : [a,b] \to \mathbb{R}^{m}$ is integrable. Then
   $$\int_a^b f' \;=\; f(b) - f(a).$$
2. **A bounded derivative gives a Lipschitz function.** Let
   $f : [a,b] \to \mathbb{R}^{m}$ be continuous on $[a,b]$ and differentiable at
   every point of $(a,b)$, and let $M \ge 0$ satisfy
   $\lVert f'(t)\rVert_2 \le M$ for every $t \in (a,b)$. Then
   $$\lVert f(t) - f(s)\rVert_2 \;\le\; M\,|t-s| \qquad \text{for all } s,t \in [a,b],$$
   that is, $f$ is Lipschitz with constant $M$ as a map
   $([a,b], d_{\mathbb{R}}) \to (\mathbb{R}^{m}, d_2)$
   ([[def-lipschitz-holder-contraction]], [[lem-real-line-is-a-metric-space]],
   [[lem-metrics-on-rn]]).

Let $m \in \mathbb{N}$ with $m \ge 1$, let $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$ with $a \le b$
and let $f : [a,b] \to \mathbb{R}^{m}$. If $a<b$, assume that $f$ is integrable
([[def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral]]). Then:

1. if $a < b$, the real-valued function $t \mapsto \lVert f(t)\rVert_2$ is
   integrable on $[a,b]$ ([[def-darboux-integral]], [[def-p-norms-on-rn]]);
2. $$\Bigl\lVert \int_a^b f \Bigr\rVert_2 \;\le\; \int_a^b \lVert f\rVert_2 .$$

**The hypothesis $a \le b$ is not decoration.** With the orientation convention
of [[def-oriented-integral]] and
[[def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral]], interchanging the limits changes
the sign of the right-hand side but not of the left, so for $b < a$ the correct
statement is $\bigl\lVert\int_a^b f\bigr\rVert_2 \le \bigl|\int_a^b \lVert f\rVert_2\bigr|$;
the displayed inequality as written is false in that case. This is the same trap
the scalar inequality of
[[cor-integrability-of-absolute-values-products-and-lattice-operations]] carries.

**Clause 1 is a genuine obligation and is discharged before the estimate.** That
each $f_i$ is integrable does not by itself say that
$\sqrt{\sum_{i<m} f_i^{2}}$ is; the square root has to be brought in through
[[thm-composition-with-a-continuous-function]].

derivations.claim: Let $R_hu(t)$ denote the face samples and $R_hp(t),R_hf(t)$ the cell and face samples, respectively. For a face array $z$, write $\bar z_i$ for the discrete mean of component $i$ repeated on every $i$-face. The input force is $f_h(t)=R_hf(t)-\bar{R_hf(t)}$, so [F3] gives $\|f_h(t)-R_hf(t)\|_{M_h}\le C h^2$. Define the sampling residual $$ r_h(t)=R_hu_t(t)+\nu A_hR_hu(t)+G_hR_hp(t)-R_hf(t). $$ The continuous Stokes equation and [F3] imply $\|r_h(t)\|_{M_h}\le C h^2$, uniformly in $t$.

Define $v_h(t)=P_hR_hu(t)$ and let $L_h=-\Delta_h$ on mean-zero cell arrays. All coordinate shifts commute, so $A_hG_h=G_hL_h$ and $D_hA_h=L_hD_h$. Since $L_h=-\Delta_h$, it commutes with $\Delta_h^{-1}$ on $Q_h$. Substitution in $P_h=I-G_h\Delta_h^{-1}D_h$ gives $P_hA_h=A_hP_h$. Also $P_hG_hq=0$ for every mean-zero $q$, because $G_hq$ is orthogonal to $\ker D_h$ by the adjoint relation in [F1]. Applying $P_h$ to the residual equation in step 1.1 therefore yields $$ v_h'(t)+\nu A_hv_h(t)=P_hf_h(t)+\rho_h(t), $$ where $\rho_h=P_hr_h+P_h(R_hf-f_h)$. By [F1], $\|P_h\|\le1$, and hence $\|\rho_h(t)\|_{M_h}\le C h^2$.

Applying $P_h$ to the predictor equation and using $P_hA_h=A_hP_h$ and $P_hG_hp_h^n=0$ shows that the actual corrected velocity is exactly the backward-Euler step on $Z_h=\ker D_h$: $$ (I+k\nu A_h)u_h^{n+1}=u_h^n+kP_hf_h(t_{n+1}). $$ The projected reference $v_h$ obeys the differential equation in step 2.1.

Put $e_h^n=u_h^n-v_h(t_n)$. Integrating $v_h'$ over $[t_n,t_{n+1}]$ and using the equation in step 2.1 gives $$ (I+k\nu A_h)v_h(t_{n+1}) =v_h(t_n)+kP_hf_h(t_{n+1})+k\rho_h(t_{n+1})+\tau_h^{n+1}, $$ where $\tau_h^{n+1}=v_h(t_{n+1})-v_h(t_n)-kv_h'(t_{n+1})$. By [F7], $$\tau_h^{n+1}=\int_{t_n}^{t_{n+1}}\bigl(v_h'(s)-v_h'(t_{n+1})\bigr)\,ds.$$ The bounded-derivative clause of [F7] gives $\|v_h'(s)-v_h'(t_{n+1})\|_{M_h}\le (t_{n+1}-s)\sup_t\|v_h''(t)\|_{M_h}$ after the isometric identification $v\mapsto h^{d/2}v$ with Euclidean coordinates. Applying [F8] yields $$\|\tau_h^{n+1}\|_{M_h}\le\int_{t_n}^{t_{n+1}}(t_{n+1}-s)\sup_t\|v_h''(t)\|_{M_h}\,ds=\frac{k^2}{2}\sup_t\|v_h''(t)\|_{M_h}\le Ck^2,$$ because $P_h$ is a contraction and $h^dN^d=1$ bounds the weighted sample norm by the continuous supremum norm up to the fixed component factor.

For any face vector $z$, periodic summation by parts gives $(A_hz,z)_{M_h}\ge0$. Hence $$ \|(I+k
u A_h)z\|_{M_h}^2 =\|z\|_{M_h}^2+2k
u(A_hz,z)_{M_h}+k^2
u^2\|A_hz\|_{M_h}^2 \ge\|z\|_{M_h}^2. $$ Thus $(I+k
u A_h)^{-1}$ is a contraction. Subtracting the equations in steps 3.1–4.1 and applying this contraction gives $$ \|e_h^{n+1}\|_{M_h} \le\|e_h^n\|_{M_h}+Ckh^2+Ck^2. $$ Since $e_h^0=0$ and $M=T/k$, summing yields $\max_n\|e_h^n\|_{M_h}\le C_T(h^2+k)$.

Finally, $u_h^n-R_hu(t_n)=e_h^n+(P_hR_hu(t_n)-R_hu(t_n))$. The second term equals $-G_h\phi$ with $\phi=\Delta_h^{-1}D_hR_hu(t_n)$. By [F4] and [F5], $$ \|G_h\phi\|_{M_h}^2 =-(\phi,\Delta_h\phi)_{Q_h} =-(\phi,D_hR_hu)_{Q_h} \le\sqrt d\|G_h\phi\|_{M_h}\|D_hR_hu\|_{Q_h}. $$ If $G_h\phi=0$ the bound is immediate; otherwise divide by its norm. Since $\nabla\cdot u=0$, [F3] gives $\|D_hR_hu\|_{Q_h}\le Ch^2$, so the projection-sampling discrepancy is $O(h^2)$. Combining this with step 5.1 proves the stated estimate.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $d\in\{2,3\}$ and let $D\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a nonempty bounded connected Lipschitz open set, where Lipschitz means that $\partial D$ has a finite rigidly moved graph-chart atlas. Here $H^1_0(D)$ is the $H^1$-closure of $C_c^\infty(D)$ ([[def-wkp-zero-as-a-sobolev-closure]], [[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]). Since $D$ has finite measure, Holder makes every $L^2$ class integrable, so the zero-mean condition is well-defined ([[thm-holder-inequality-for-integrals]]). Define
$$V:=H^1_0(D;\mathbb R^d),\qquad Q:=L^2_0(D):=\{q\in L^2(D;\mathbb R):\int_Dq=0\}.$$
Equip $V$ with $\|v\|_V:=\|
abla v\|_{L^2(D)}$ and $Q$ with $\|q\|_Q:=\|q\|_{L^2(D)}$. The local Poincare inequality [[lem-na-homogeneous-dirichlet-poincare]] makes the first a norm equivalent to the usual $H^1$ norm. For $v\in V$, define $\varepsilon(v):=(
abla v+
abla v^T)/2$ and $b(v,q):=-\int_Dq\,\operatorname{div}v$. For viscosity $
u>0$, set $a_
u(u,v):=2
u\int_D\varepsilon(u):\varepsilon(v)$, where $X:Y=\sum_{i,j}X_{ij}Y_{ij}$. The continuous domain class is all bounded connected Lipschitz $D$; the exact mini-element mesh class is the narrower polygonal/polyhedral conforming affine simplicial class.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $D\subset\mathbb R^d$, $d=2$ or $3$, be a bounded connected Lipschitz polygonal/polyhedral domain with a conforming shape-regular affine simplicial mesh $\mathcal T_h$. On a simplex $K$ with barycentric coordinates $\lambda_0,\ldots,\lambda_d$, define the scalar interior bubble $b_K=(d+1)^{d+1}\prod_{i=0}^d\lambda_i$. Let
$$S^1_h=\{w\in C^0(\overline D):w|_K\in P_1(K)\},\quad S^1_{h,0}=S^1_h\cap H^1_0(D).$$
The **mini-element spaces** are
$$V_h=[S^1_{h,0}]^d\oplus\bigoplus_{K\in\mathcal T_h}b_K\mathbb R^d\subset H^1_0(D;\mathbb R^d),\qquad Q_h=S^1_h\cap L^2_0(D).$$
Each bubble is extended by zero off its cell. The zero-boundary conformity of the piecewise affine part is supplied by [[thm-zero-boundary-piecewise-polynomials-in-w10p]]. The local/global dimensions are proved in the next dimension lemma.

Assume Countable Choice. For a nonempty connected conforming simplicial mesh in dimension $d=2$ or $3$, the local scalar velocity polynomial space $P_1(K)\oplus\operatorname{span}\{b_K\}$ has dimension $d+2$, the vector velocity dimension is $d(d+2)$, and the local pressure space $P_1(K)$ has dimension $d+1$. If the mesh has $N_v$ vertices, $N_{v,0}$ interior vertices and $N_K$ cells, then
$$\dim V_h=dN_{v,0}+dN_K,\qquad \dim Q_h=N_v-1.$$

Assume Countable Choice. For bounded open $D\subset\mathbb R^d$ and $v\in H^1_0(D;\mathbb R^d)$, put $\varepsilon(v)=(
abla v+
abla v^T)/2$. Then
$$2\|\varepsilon(v)\|_2^2=\|
abla v\|_2^2+\|\operatorname{div}v\|_2^2,$$
so $\|
abla v\|_2\le\sqrt2\|\varepsilon(v)\|_2$.

On the mini-element spaces of [[def-na-mini-element-p1-bubble-p1-spaces]], there is a Fortin operator $\Pi_h:V\to V_h$ preserving $b(v,q_h)$ for every $q_h\in Q_h$, with $\|\Pi_hv\|_V\le C_F\|v\|_V$. The constant depends only on $d$ and the mesh shape-regularity bound, not on $h$. Consequently
$$\beta_h\ge (C_FC_{\rm div}(D))^{-1}.$$

Let $V,Q$ be finite-dimensional real inner-product spaces with norms
$\|\cdot\|_V,\|\cdot\|_Q$. Let $a(v,w)=v^TAw$ be symmetric positive
definite, and let $b(v,q)=q^TBv$ be a bilinear constraint form, represented
by the matrices in
[[def-na-symmetric-saddle-point-system-and-block-preconditioners]]. Suppose
that, for constants $\alpha,\Lambda,C_b,\beta>0$,
$$ \alpha\|v\|_V^2\le a(v,v)\le\Lambda\|v\|_V^2, \quad |b(v,q)|\le C_b\|v\|_V\|q\|_Q, \quad \sup_{v\ne0}\frac{|b(v,q)|}{\|v\|_V}\ge\beta\|q\|_Q. $$

to the unique element of $\{0,\ldots,N-1\}$ congruent modulo $N$. The unit
torus $\mathbb T^d$ means the unit cube with opposite faces identified, so
fields and arrays are periodic across those faces. Write
$\mathbf 1=(1,\ldots,1)$ and let $e_i$ be the $i$th standard coordinate vector.
Cell $j$ has centre $x_j=h(j+\tfrac12\mathbf 1)$. The pressure value $q_j$ is
stored at that centre. Velocity component $i$ is stored at the right face of
cell $j$, with centre $x_j+\tfrac h2e_i$.

Let $\widetilde Q_h$ be all real scalar cell arrays and let
$Q_h=\{q\in\widetilde Q_h:h^d\sum_jq_j=0\}$. Let $V_h$ be the real vector
face arrays $v=(v_{i,j})_{1\le i\le d,\,j\in J_N}$. Give them the mass inner products
$$ (q,r)_{Q_h}=h^d\sum_{j\in J_N}q_jr_j,\qquad (v,w)_{M_h}=h^d\sum_{i=1}^d\sum_{j\in J_N}v_{i,j}w_{i,j}. $$
Define the pressure gradient $G_h:\widetilde Q_h\to V_h$ and velocity
divergence $D_h:V_h\to Q_h$ by
$$ (G_hq)_{i,j}=\frac{q_{j+e_i}-q_j}{h},\qquad (D_hv)_j=\sum_{i=1}^d\frac{v_{i,j}-v_{i,j-e_i}}{h}. $$
The compatible pressure Laplacian is $\Delta_h=D_hG_h$; its restriction to
$Q_h$ is negative semidefinite, and $G_h$ annihilates constants. Define the
componentwise vector Laplacian by
$$ (\Delta_h^Vv)_{i,j}=h^{-2}\sum_{\ell=1}^d (v_{i,j+e_\ell}-2v_{i,j}+v_{i,j-e_\ell}),\qquad A_h=-\Delta_h^V, $$
and the discrete velocity-gradient seminorm by
$$ \|\mathcal G_hv\|_{M_h}^2=h^{d-2}\sum_{i=1}^d\sum_{\ell=1}^d\sum_{j\in J_N} |v_{i,j+e_\ell}-v_{i,j}|^2. $$

differences are a different discretization.

Let $n,m\ge1$, $V=M_{n\times1}(\mathbb R)$, and
$Q=M_{m\times1}(\mathbb R)$. Let $A\in M_n(\mathbb R)$ be symmetric
positive definite, let $B\in M_{m\times n}(\mathbb R)$ have full row rank
(meaning $B^Tq=0$ implies $q=0$), and let
$M_Q\in M_m(\mathbb R)$ be symmetric positive definite. The saddle system
and its matrix are
$$ K=\begin{pmatrix}A&B^T\\B&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad Au+B^Tp=f,\quad Bu=g. $$
Define the positive pressure Schur matrix
$$ S:=BA^{-1}B^T. $$
In the block-LU convention of [[def-block-lu-factorisation]], the trailing
Schur complement of $A$ in $K$ is $-S$. The exact block solve first solves
$Au_0=f$, then $Sp=Bu_0-g$, and finally $Au=f-B^Tp$; the theorem
[[thm-na-saddle-point-exact-schur-solve]] verifies this procedure and
well-definedness.

For a scaling $\gamma>0$, the pressure-mass block-diagonal preconditioner is
$$ P_\gamma=\operatorname{diag}(A,\gamma M_Q). $$
It is symmetric positive definite. If $P_\gamma=CC^T$ is its Cholesky
factorization with $C$ lower triangular and positive on the diagonal, the
symmetric preconditioned system is $C^{-1}KC^{-T}y=C^{-1}r$, with the usual
change of unknown. This is the symmetric-preconditioning convention of
[[def-left-right-and-symmetric-positive-definite-preconditioning]]. No
spectral bound, Krylov iteration count, complexity estimate, or generic speed
improvement is part of this definition.

Assume the hypotheses and Schur bounds of
[[thm-na-pressure-schur-spectral-equivalence-from-infsup]], with constants
$\alpha,\Lambda,C_b,\beta>0$. For $\gamma>0$, use
$P_\gamma=\operatorname{diag}(A,\gamma M_Q)$ from
[[def-na-symmetric-saddle-point-system-and-block-preconditioners]], and set
$$ a_\gamma=\frac{\beta^2}{\Lambda\gamma},\qquad b_\gamma=\frac{C_b^2}{\alpha\gamma},\qquad \lambda_\pm(s)=\frac{1\pm\sqrt{1+4s}}2. $$
Let $\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_m$ be the eigenvalues, with multiplicity, of
$(\gamma M_Q)^{-1/2}S(\gamma M_Q)^{-1/2}$. Then
$a_\gamma\le\mu_j\le b_\gamma$, and the symmetric square-root-preconditioned
saddle matrix has eigenvalues
$$ \{\lambda_-(\mu_j),\lambda_+(\mu_j):1\le j\le m\} \quad\text{and }1\text{ with multiplicity }n-m. $$
Consequently its spectrum is contained in
$$ [\lambda_-(b_\gamma),\lambda_-(a_\gamma)]\;\cup\; \{1\}\;\cup\; [\lambda_+(a_\gamma),\lambda_+(b_\gamma)], $$
where the eigenvalue $1$ has multiplicity zero if $n=m$. This is a spectral
estimate for the stated scaled block preconditioner, not an iteration-count
or generic solver-speed claim.

derivations.claim: The scalar matrix $A=[1]$ is SPD, $B^Tq=0$ implies $q=0$, and the Schur matrix is $S=BA^{-1}B^T=[1]$. Thus the normalized Schur eigenvalue is $\mu=1$ and $P_1=\operatorname{diag}(1,1)=I$ by [F1].

Applying [F2] at $\mu=1$ gives the characteristic polynomial $\lambda^2-\lambda-1$ and roots $(1\pm\sqrt5)/2$. Direct substitution in $u+p=1$ and $u=0$ yields $(u,p)=(0,1)$; the coefficient matrix is invertible because its determinant is $-1$, so this solution is unique.

Fix an integer dimension $d\ge1$ and an integer resolution $N\ge2$, where
$N\in\mathbb N$ ([[def-natural-numbers]]), and put $h=1/N$. Real scalar and
array operations use the field $\mathbb R$ ([[thm-reals-field]]). Let
$J_N=\{0,\ldots,N-1\}^d$; each coordinate index addition below is reduced
to the unique element of $\{0,\ldots,N-1\}$ congruent modulo $N$. The unit
torus $\mathbb T^d$ means the unit cube with opposite faces identified, so
fields and arrays are periodic across those faces. Write
$\mathbf 1=(1,\ldots,1)$ and let $e_i$ be the $i$th standard coordinate vector.
Cell $j$ has centre $x_j=h(j+\tfrac12\mathbf 1)$. The pressure value $q_j$ is
stored at that centre. Velocity component $i$ is stored at the right face of
cell $j$, with centre $x_j+\tfrac h2e_i$.

Let $\widetilde Q_h$ be all real scalar cell arrays and let
$Q_h=\{q\in\widetilde Q_h:h^d\sum_jq_j=0\}$. Let $V_h$ be the real vector
face arrays $v=(v_{i,j})_{1\le i\le d,\,j\in J_N}$. Give them the mass inner products
$$ (q,r)_{Q_h}=h^d\sum_{j\in J_N}q_jr_j,\qquad (v,w)_{M_h}=h^d\sum_{i=1}^d\sum_{j\in J_N}v_{i,j}w_{i,j}. $$
Define the pressure gradient $G_h:\widetilde Q_h\to V_h$ and velocity
divergence $D_h:V_h\to Q_h$ by
$$ (G_hq)_{i,j}=\frac{q_{j+e_i}-q_j}{h},\qquad (D_hv)_j=\sum_{i=1}^d\frac{v_{i,j}-v_{i,j-e_i}}{h}. $$
The compatible pressure Laplacian is $\Delta_h=D_hG_h$; its restriction to
$Q_h$ is negative semidefinite, and $G_h$ annihilates constants. Define the
componentwise vector Laplacian by
$$ (\Delta_h^Vv)_{i,j}=h^{-2}\sum_{\ell=1}^d (v_{i,j+e_\ell}-2v_{i,j}+v_{i,j-e_\ell}),\qquad A_h=-\Delta_h^V, $$
and the discrete velocity-gradient seminorm by
$$ \|\mathcal G_hv\|_{M_h}^2=h^{d-2}\sum_{i=1}^d\sum_{\ell=1}^d\sum_{j\in J_N} |v_{i,j+e_\ell}-v_{i,j}|^2. $$
The fixed cell/face placement is part of the definition; collocated central
differences are a different discretization.

Fix $d\ge1$, $N\ge2$, $h=1/N$, viscosity $\nu>0$, and time step $k>0$.
Given $u^n\in V_h$ with $D_hu^n=0$, a mean-zero
pressure $p^n\in Q_h$, and a force $f^{n+1}\in V_h$ whose components each
have zero discrete mean,
$$h^d\sum_{j\in J_N}f_{i,j}^{n+1}=0\qquad(1\le i\le d),$$
define the next step by the following two solves and update:

1. Find $\widetilde u^{n+1}\in V_h$ satisfying
$$ \frac{\widetilde u^{n+1}-u^n}{k}+\nu A_h\widetilde u^{n+1}+G_hp^n=f^{n+1}. $$

2. Find the unique $\phi^{n+1}\in Q_h$ satisfying
$$ \Delta_h\phi^{n+1}=k^{-1}D_h\widetilde u^{n+1}. $$

3. Set
$$ u^{n+1}=\widetilde u^{n+1}-kG_h\phi^{n+1},\qquad p^{n+1}=p^n+\phi^{n+1}. $$

The pressure is kept in $Q_h$ after every solve; the constant pressure mode
is set to zero. The procedure is only asserted for the periodic staggered
grid and the admissible data stated here. The separate well-definedness
theorem [[thm-na-periodic-pressure-correction-solves-well-defined]] verifies
both solves and the preserved constraints.

On the periodic staggered grid of
[[def-na-periodic-staggered-grid-stokes-operators]], every admissible backward-
Euler step of [[alg-na-periodic-incremental-pressure-correction]] and every
admissible BDF2 step of
[[alg-na-bdf2-incremental-and-rotational-pressure-correction]] has a unique
predictor, a unique mean-zero pressure increment, and a unique updated pair.
Both algorithms preserve the zero-mean pressure gauge and exact discrete
incompressibility.

On the grid of [[def-na-periodic-staggered-grid-stokes-operators]], let
$\Delta_h^{-1}:Q_h\to Q_h$ be the inverse from
[[lem-na-periodic-grid-pressure-laplacian-zero-mode-and-poincare]]. Define
$$ P_h:=I-G_h\Delta_h^{-1}D_h:V_h\to V_h. $$
Then $P_h$ is the mass-orthogonal projector onto
$Z_h=\ker D_h$. In the backward-Euler algorithm
[[alg-na-periodic-incremental-pressure-correction]], the velocity correction
satisfies $u^{n+1}=P_h\widetilde u^{n+1}$ and
$D_hu^{n+1}=0$ exactly.

derivations.claim: Since $N$ is even, $q$ has zero mean. The staggered gradient is not zero: $(G_hq)_{1,j}=-2q_j/h$. Also $\Delta_hq=-4q/h^2$, so [F1] gives $D_hG_hq=\Delta_hq$. Periodic summation shows both $G_hq$ and $A_hG_hq$ have zero component means, hence the force is admissible.

Substituting $\widetilde u^{n+1}=G_hq$ and $u^n=p^n=0$ into the predictor equation [F2] gives $k^{-1}G_hq+\nu A_hG_hq=f^{n+1}$, so uniqueness [F3] identifies it as the predictor. For the pressure equation, $$ \Delta_h(k^{-1}q)=k^{-1}D_hG_hq=k^{-1}D_h\widetilde u^{n+1}; $$ both sides have mean zero and [F3] gives $\phi^{n+1}=k^{-1}q$.
The velocity update [F2] now gives $u^{n+1}=G_hq-kG_h(k^{-1}q)=0$, while the pressure update gives $p^{n+1}=k^{-1}q$. This is exact one-step removal of the selected mode.
